transcript: I'm gonna rank all 10 Jamie Lloyd productions that I've seen easily in last place I have Romeo and Juliet where he made some bold but misguided choices that didn't serve the text didn't illuminate anything in the text so it ended up just being a big misfire next I have Cyrano de Bergerac which I know a lot of people really liked I did actually think it was brilliantly conceived in terms of how they were using rap and spoken word poetry but this is a play that I really love for how tender and sentimental it is and I found this production very cold And whatever he was playing around with by casting this traditionally handsome celebrity as Cyrano it didn't resonate with me quick warning the next one on this ranking is gonna be my most controversial but stick with me because my specific reasoning is important so with Sunset Boulevard I actually liked the vast majority of Jamie Lloyd's direction But at least half of what it takes to put on a good revival is choice of material and I find this material so unbearable like nails on a chalkboard to me like if they had commissioned a new adaptation of this story and done everything else exactly the same I probably would have loved it in 7th place I have this 2017 revival of the Pitchfork Disney which was performed in this narrow corridor in the basement of Shoreditch Town Hall possibly his most striking use of space and definitely this raw gut punch with the play’s somewhat grotesque and upsetting content but his direction here maybe lacked some of the dramatic finesse of his best work In 6th place his newest offering, Waiting for Godot there's a lot that I liked about it but for a production built around this leading pair of actors I don't think it played to their strengths and their performances just didn't work well enough for me getting into more solidly positive territory I have the recent revival of Lucy Brebble’s The Effrct and I don't think Jamie Lloyd did anything really radical with the text here but it was just beautifully directed similarly I have his production of The Homecoming by Harold Pinter and yes that's Gemma Chan in the cast she wasn't as famous back then, I don't think This is before Jamie Lloyd got really abstract and experimental but there was still a fresh, modern feel to the production and he perfectly captured the tension and strange dark comedy in the play in 3rd place much ado about nothing not only was this a delightful production of my favorite Shakespeare comedy I also think Jamie Lloyd's skillset allowed him to take the sort of dark turn in the second half and make it feel more tonally coherent like the tone didn't clash as much as it does in a lot of productions of this play potentially another very hot take for 2nd place I have A Doll's House which I know was not everyone's cup of tea but I don't know what to tell you I was just completely on the edge of my seat like you could cut the tension with a knife and I thought Jessica Chastain was brilliant but in first place I have Betrayal which I actually got to see in London and on Broadway and I think the 2nd time I appreciated it a lot more a lot of what I said about A Doll’s House I think applies to this one too except it's a play that I like more I think I emotionally resonate with it more so that's my ranking but what do you guys think? like aside from Sunset Boulevard what would you do differently? especially for people in London what were your favorite Jamie Lloyd productions that I didn't get to see?
